title: Ampelovirus Coverage Audit
h1: Does the grapevine leafroll-associated virus 3 module actually work?
standfirst: Ampelovirus is the mealybug-transmitted genus of the Closteroviridae, dominated by grapevine leafroll-associated virus 3 — one of the most economically damaging grapevine viruses in the world. Same gene block as Closterovirus, a different accessory set.

sections.title: What the module covers
sections.lede: Eleven features: five core plus CPm, and five accessories including the p20A/p20B pair.

blocks.html: Self-recall is a floor, not a validation: a profile that cannot recover its own training data will certainly not recover anything new, but recovering it proves very little. The held-out numbers are in §05 and §06.

sections.title: How it was built
sections.lede: Binned from the BV-BRC protein dump, with the accessory names treated as untrustworthy.

blocks.html: The accessories are named by mass, and a mass is not a homology group. Where two masses turned out to be one protein they were merged; where one mass covered two non-homologous groups they were numbered apart.
400 for the replicase polyprotein, 300 for the RdRp, 150 for the HSP70 and HSP90 homologs, 80 for the coat proteins, 25–60 for the accessories by length.
89.5% at the 25-reference budget, the lowest of the three closterovirid modules and a documented gap rather than a defect — the genus is large and unevenly sampled.

sections.title: Does it call the proteins?
sections.lede: Measured against real genomes for the first time.

blocks.html: No correction was needed. The five essential features measure 93.2–99.3% and the six accessories 37.0–63.0%, so every copy_num assignment in the shipped module was already right. CPM is genuinely absent from a third of the genus.

41 of the 52 flags are “too many HSPs” and 20 a missing essential feature — the latter consistent with essentials calling at 93–99% rather than 100%. “Genome has too many HSPs” is the dominant flag, and it is a different thing from a duplicate call: it means one feature's profile matched at several places in a genome, not that two features collided. The duplicate-call audit is clean for this module.
p20A and p20B share a mass and are not the same protein. They are numbered rather than merged, and that is the precedent every later module followed: a mass is a name, not a homology group.
Routing is 89.5%, so roughly one genome in ten of the genus is not reached by the shipped reference set.

The evaluation is a sample. Measured on a random sample of up to 150 genomes at ≥6 kb (seed 29). Annotation costs about 86 seconds per genome, and 150 is ample for the decision it feeds: the test for copy_num is whether a feature is called on at least 85% of routed genomes, estimated to within about ±6 points at that sample size.

The homology rescue has never run on this module, and should be re-done. Deferred 30 September 2026 by the curator, not forgotten. Step 2 bins proteins by their annotation string; rescue_unassigned.py takes everything no string rule matched, blastp’s it against this module's own collections and adopts each sequence into the feature it matches at ≥80% identity over ≥60% of the query. It recovers exactly the sequences a string rule cannot reach — hypothetical protein, masses like 64kDa protein, positional labels like ORF3, and outright typos (Polypretein, Coat prtein) — and it refuses everything below threshold rather than sweeping it into an uncharacterized bag. Measured here: 1185 sequences matched no rule and 679 would be adopted, against 2274 currently binned — about 30% more training data. Until it runs, this module's profiles are built from a collection missing that fraction of its own taxon, and the population missing is the divergent one: on Alpharhabdovirinae, 85 of 85 genomes with an uncalled P had a full-length, correct-looking gene that resembled a leftover sequence and none that resembled a clustered one. Neither self-recall nor a reference panel shows this.

Three features are mass bins holding more than one homology group, and must be split. P7 (five groups: GLRaV-3 47 | GLRaV-1 29 | three GLRaV-13 groups of 3), P21 (GLRaV-3 with PMWaV-6 40 | GLRaV-1 38) and P24 (GLRaV-1 42 | SCMMV 11 | PMWaV 9). No pair of groups shares a blastp HSP at 1e-3. A bin must be one homology group; until these are split each calls two or more different proteins under one key. Deferred alongside the rescue, because splitting forces a build_collections re-run that discards a rescue — the two are one job.
Nothing. This is the only one of the three closterovirid modules that needed no change when it was finally measured, and that is worth recording as plainly as the modules that did.
Eleven of eleven features have profiles, self-recall 97.0–100%, five essential on measurement, and no correction required.
The module's vocabulary is complete after four genomes; the source reaches 164 distinct strings with its knee at 122.
